source_title: Successful Non-Transplant Treatment of Double Hit Richter Transformation with Long-Term Remission
disease_label_per_paper: Double-hit Richter transformation after standard-risk chronic lymphocytic leukemia
presentation_summary: Rai stage I standard-risk CLL was observed with watchful waiting for about five years
The patient then developed progressive worsening pelvic pain over three weeks
Laboratory workup showed WBC 10.8 x10^9/L, ALC 1.28 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL, platelets 153 x10^9/L, and LDH 256 U/L with reference 122-222 U/L
CT showed a new 7.6 cm left pelvic sidewall mass, hypermetabolic on PET, with left hydronephrosis and increased pelvic mesenteric and external iliac lymphadenopathy
Pelvic mass biopsy showed high-grade B-cell lymphoma coexisting with CLL in the same tumor and FISH confirmed MYC and BCL6 rearrangements
He received anthracycline-based and platinum-based chemoimmunotherapy, intrathecal methotrexate prophylaxis, and continuous ibrutinib maintenance, achieving long-term complete remission

observations.source_text_value: standard-risk CLL followed by about 5 years of watchful waiting
progressive worsening of pelvic pain over a period of 3 weeks
LDH 256 U/L with upper reference 222 U/L
increased pelvic mesenteric lymphadenopathy and external iliac lymphadenopathy
new pelvic sidewall mass plus increased pelvic mesenteric and external iliac lymphadenopathy
progressive pelvic pain over 3 weeks with new 7.6 cm pelvic sidewall mass
new left pelvic sidewall mass 7.6 cm in maximum transverse dimension
left pelvic sidewall mass 7.6 cm in maximum transverse dimension
the mass was hypermetabolic on PET, but SUV could not be accurately measured
associated left hydronephrosis from involved left ureter

confirmatory_findings.finding: CT-guided core biopsy of the pelvic mass showed large atypical cells with intermixed small lymphocytes, supporting Richter transformation in the same tumor
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: CT-guided core biopsy of the pelvic mass showed diffusely infiltrating large atypical cells with intermixed clusters of small lymphocytes

confirmatory_findings.finding: FISH confirmed MYC and BCL6 rearrangements, establishing double-hit large B-cell lymphoma in the Richter transformation
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: FISH analysis with break-apart probes demonstrated MYC gene rearrangement and BCL6 gene rearrangement

pathology.diagnosis: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL6 rearrangements coexisting with CLL in the same tumor
immunophenotype: Small and large lymphocytes strongly positive for CD20
Small lymphocytes aberrantly expressed CD5 and CD23
Large lymphocytes negative for CD5 and CD23, positive for BCL6, with high Ki-67

infection_exclusion_context.details: The case report did not describe fever or a separate infectious exclusion workup at transformation presentation.

actual_treatment: Complete remission after induction and ongoing remission at four and a half years
quality_warnings: FISH, IHC, and biopsy results are confirmation/pathology and are not ordinary ranking observations.
SUV max was not measured because of concentrated radiotracer in the involved left ureter.
Clonal relatedness molecular testing was not performed; the paper inferred likely relatedness from coexistence of CLL and double-hit RT in the same tumor.
